name: Question 8
problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $b$ shown above. If the general least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}a \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R
$$

what is the value of $a+2b+c?$
worked_solution:
The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}6 & -8 & 2 \\ -8 & 12 & -4 \\ 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the final matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -8 & 2 & 0 \\ -8 & 12 & -4 & 2 \\ 2 & -4 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 2 & -2 \\ -8 & 12 & -4 & 2 \\ 6 & -8 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & -4 & 4 & -6 \\ 0 & 4 & -4 & 6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & -4 & 4 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{2}=\frac{3}{2}+{x}_{3}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
2{x}_{1}-4(\frac{3}{2}+{x}_{3})+2{x}_{3}=-2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2+{x}_{3}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}2+{x}_{3} \\ \frac{3}{2}+{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{3}{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+2b+c=1+2\cdot \frac{3}{2}+0=4.
$$

EXPLANATION

The least-squares solution of Ax=b satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

ATAx=ATb

Notice that the columns of A are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

[1−12−22−21−10][1−21−12−12−20][x1x2x3]=[1−12−22−21−10][−201][6−82−812−42−42][x1x2x3]=[02−2].

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the final matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

M=[6−820−812−422−42−2]R1↔R3∼[2−42−2−812−426−820]R2:=R2+4R1R3:=R3+(−3)R1∼[2−42−20−44−604−46]R3:=R3+(−1)R2∼[2−42−20−44−60000]

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the 1st and 2nd). Thus, x3 is a free variable. From the second equation, we have x2=32+x3. Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain 2x1−4(32+x3)+2x3=−2⟹x1=2+x3. Hence, the general solution is

[2+x332+x3x3]=[2320]+x3[111],x3∈R.

Therefore, we have

a+2b+c=1+2⋅32+0=4.
